analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md: the date bump on line 3 and a new paragraph in the `inference_response_chunk` section (head lines 757-765) describing streamed `auto` tool-call chunking. No executable code, protocol parsing, key handling, authorization, or encryption behavior changes.

The new paragraph describes OpenAI-style streamed `choices[].delta.tool_calls`, with the first fragment carrying id/type/name and later fragments carrying `function.arguments`, keyed by `index`. It does not change the wire envelope, `encrypted_data` handling, or T-008 fail-closed behavior. It is consistent with T-008 and A-001, since the content is still carried in chunks whose plaintext `data` is empty when E2E encryption is active. The chunk-level `data` empty rule in the field table at line 754 is unchanged.

In units 7 and 8 (head lines 1-583) I saw no other diff-affected content. The wider document (App Attest resume, drain barrier, prefix-cache telemetry) is unchanged context. It remains consistent with TB-011, T-053 and T-041, and nothing in it is loosened, such as the TTL, endpoint binding or non-bearer semantics.

Remaining unverified: the referenced architecture anchor (`inference.md#streamed-auto-tool-calls`) and the Swift source `MLXOpenAIService.swift` are not supplied. Whether tool-call fragments are properly encrypted per chunk is outside this diff and was not checked. The documentation claims are unverified against that code, but a docs-only change is not a security regression.
